correctness.rationale: For every finite field and every distinct evaluation set with the exact triple nonvanishing condition, the two generalized Vandermonde determinants are the ordinary Vandermonde factor times e_1 or e_2, proving the arc/MDS premise. The dimension-three projective conic criterion is proved and properly specialized. The quadratic-monomial exponents are {0,1,2,3,4,6} for r=1 and {0,2,3,4,5,6} for r=2; the six-root polynomial uniquely certifies the e_1/e_5 test, and a degree-six root bound excludes seven or more coordinates. Five arc points lie on a unique smooth conic. For each five-set, the e_1 extension equation has one possible root; the e_5 extension equation has coefficients (e_4,e_5) not both zero since the evaluations are distinct, proving the five-packing. An exact F_19 arc/conic certificate refutes a non-GRS assertion at n=2k=6. The bundled verify.py independently computes modular conic ranks on all relevant small prime-field sets, checks direct conic equations and both deletion regimes, and concludes VERIFY_OK. Finite checks are not claimed as an infinite proof. Boundary n>=5, initial n>=7 for the puncturing distance, and characteristics including two are treated.

originality.rationale: Closest full-text sources were compared by implication. Ning arXiv:2507.04689 defines and analyzes the same missing-monomial evaluation codes but gives self-dual, NMDS and dual descriptions, not the complete punctured GRS profile. Jin et al. arXiv:2411.14779 Proposition VI.1 proves the known strict n>2k non-GRS part; their Proposition V.1 also asserts non-GRS at n=2k=6 for r=1, but the explicit p=19 MDS six-point conic refutes that equality case. Abdukhalikov--Ding--Verma arXiv:2506.04080 Theorem 3.2 asserts non-GRS already at n>=2k; at equality the explicit p=19 six-coordinate MDS arc lying on a smooth conic contradicts that assertion, so this asserted coverage is false at the precise boundary. Classical conic/GRS equivalence by Marquez-Corbella--Pellikaan supplies a method, but no inspected relevant source explicitly implies the e_1/e_5 iff conditions, sharp one-step/two-step puncturing dichotomy and six-set packing for both deleted-degree families. Recent research-record semantic queries gave no overlapping named claim. The conclusion is originality of the complete boundary classification, not of the known general recognition theorem or n>=7 non-GRS fact.
residual_risks: Unindexed, unpublished, or unexamined specialized finite-geometry literature could discuss the same six-point missing-monomial locus.
The argument assumes exactly the stated MDS triple condition and evaluation at finite-field points, not extensions or more general codes.
Disagreement with the weak-inequality non-RS statements in Jin et al. Proposition V.1 and Abdukhalikov et al. Theorem 3.2 is strictly at n=2k=6 and does not challenge the valid n>2k result.
The checker enumerates selected small prime fields, while correctness for all finite fields rests on the written proof; independent verification has not yet occurred.

value.rationale: The natural non-GRS-to-GRS transition under puncturing is a structural coding-theory question motivated by row-deleted GRS constructions and the known longer-length Schur-square obstruction. For both distinct cubic families and every finite field, the theorem gives all successful six-subset descendants, sharp deletion depths n-6 versus n-5, and an exact packing-incidence constraint on the optimal subsets. Both thresholds occur in explicit MDS examples. The equality-boundary MDS-conic witness also distinguishes the correct strict n>2k non-GRS range from published weak-inequality assertions. Thus it resolves a motivated complete boundary classification rather than computing a narrow arbitrary parameter, routine table entry, or unsupported quantitative improvement. No generalization to arbitrary MDS codes is claimed.
